- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or lagging in mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show a downward trend or mean reversion.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced when historical prices are rising — model overreacts to momentum, then underreacts to correction.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true decline.
- When true prices are near or below 70, model tends to overestimate — especially if recent history includes low values.
- Model is sensitive to recent high values — if last 5–7 days are high, forecast tends to peak higher than true outcome.
- Model often fails to capture short-term volatility — underestimates sharp drops or overestimates slow recoveries.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 1–3 day forecasts are more accurate than 30-day; model struggles with long-term smoothing.
